author: Michael Johnson
title: House Speaker Emanuel 'Chris' Welch will not seek reelection to leadership, sources tell WGN - NewsBreak
text:
By Michael Johnson Tahman Bradley ,
3 hours ago
Illinois House Speaker Emanuel "Chris" Welch will not seek reelection to his leadership post next January, sources tell WGN Political Editor Tahman Bradley.
In a statement released Thursday night, Welch said:
I have worked tirelessly to serve this House Democratic Caucus. It is one that I love, and deeply respect. I have always told the caucus that our time in this space is finite, but we are playing an infinite game. Diversity is our strength, but unity is our power. Together, we passed historic legislation on transit, cannabis and energy, and secured greater investments in education. We defended vulnerable seats and grew our majority in every election under my leadership, building a historic House Democratic majority. I am proud of this work, but I serve at the pleasure of the caucus, and I want our caucus to lead in unity and take on the mandate we received from voters this past election confidently. With that, I look forward to joining the caucus as we usher in our next leader and take our party further into the future."
The news follows 26 current and incoming members of the Illinois State House Democratic Caucus saying Wednesday night that they wouldn't support Welch continuing as House speaker. Welch has been in the role for six years.
The withdrawal of support for Welch comes in light of how he handled the sexual harassment allegations against former State Rep. Harry Benton, who resigned from his seat in July.
The investigations of those allegations also led to the resignation of Michael McCuskey , the legislature's top watchdog, amid calls from both sides of the aisle to overhaul how misconduct in the state legislature is handled.
Additionally, lawmakers have raised questions about how Welch has used his social media.
"Over the course of the last six months, we have grown increasingly convinced that the House Democratic Caucus needs new leadership," the 26 members of the caucus said in a signed letter. "We represent a broad spectrum of our caucus, and each have come to this decision for our own reasons.
"We look forward to a robust race for a new Speaker of the House."
The 26 current and incoming caucus members who signed the letter are: Rep. Diane Blair-Sherlock (46th District), Rep. Mary Beth Canty (54th), Rep. Kelly Cassidy (14th), Rep. Sharon Chung (91st), Rep. Justin Cochran (55th), Rep. Fred Crespo (44th), Rep. Margaret DeLaRosa (42nd) , Rep. Eva-Dina Delgado (3rd), Rep. Daniel Didech (59th), Rep. Jessica Dixon Heitman (97th), Rep. Mary Gill (35th), Rep. Jennifer Gong-Gershowitz (17th), Rep. Angelica Guerrero-Cuellar (22nd), Rep. Barbara Hernandez (50th), Rep. Lisa Hernandez (2nd), Rep. Gregg Johnson (72nd), Rep. Tracy Katz Muhl (57th), Rep.-Elect Paul Kendrick (12th), Rep. Natalie Manley (98th), Rep. Joyce Mason (61st), Rep. Bob Morgan (58th), Rep. Michelle Mussman (56ht), Rep.-Elect Maria Peterson (52nd), Rep. Anne Stava (81st), Rep. Katie Stuart (112th), and Rep. Larry Walsh Jr. (86th).
